criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs runs the configured checks (via the existing runner in crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs) on the producer's tree before the verifier, with GIT_INDEX_FILE set to a temporary index of the work tree. A failure's command, exit status and output tail are added to the existing send-back problems and rendered by send_back_text in crates/athena-core/src/run/send_back.rs. The stored invocation detail names the check failure.
criteria.evidence: In producer.rs:501-510, producer_loop calls Athena::loop_check_failures after each report. That function (checks.rs) runs the routed checks through SnapExec and run_check with in_loop: true. CheckFailure::problem is added to `problems`, so it goes into the stored `self-check failed: …` detail (producer.rs:584) and into report_problems. append_check_failures adds the command, exit status and tail to the text send_back_text returns (producer.rs:664-670). GIT_INDEX_FILE is set to a temporary index only for one `git add -A`; ExposedIndex then copies that index over .git/index and restores it on drop. This differs from the literal wording. D182 says so openly and gives a reason: an exported variable would break nested git calls. The planned demonstrations the critic accepted describe this design. All named tests pass, including the end-to-end test that checks the stored detail and the index/restore test.

findings.summary: One `cargo test -p athena-cli` run exited 101 while the athena-core suite ran alongside it; the failing test is unknown and a clean rerun passed
findings.evidence: The first `cargo test -p athena-cli` run, made while `cargo test -p athena-core` was running in the background, exited 101. The output was cut off partway through drain.rs, so the failing test is unknown. `cargo test -p athena-cli --no-fail-fast -- --quiet` then passed every target, and CI passed. The extra in-loop check pass adds wall time to every cli job fixture, so a timing-sensitive test may now be closer to its limit under load. This is unconfirmed.

findings.summary: An interrupted run can leave the snapshot's .git/index swapped
findings.evidence: ExposedIndex restores the saved index only in Drop. If the process is killed (SIGKILL, kill switch) during the in-loop checks, the producer snapshot's .git/index keeps the exposed index, and a resumed job's producer would see the new files as staged. This is cosmetic in most flows, because change_list and work_tree_tree use their own temporary indexes.

findings.summary: The Provenance bullet refers to the temporary-index choice instead of stating it
findings.evidence: Provenance says `The temporary-index choice is described in the Decision.` The criterion is met by this reference plus the full description in the Decision bullet.

findings.summary: The fails-without demonstration failed to compile rather than at the asserted behaviour
findings.evidence: Athena's fails-without-1/2/4 runs exited 101 because the unit tests call new functions (append_check_failures, settle_loop_checks). The end-to-end tests themselves use only test helpers and would fail at runtime on the base logic, as planned, but that was not shown separately.

summary: Verdict: pass. Before the verifier runs, Athena now runs the configured checks on the producer's tree, inside the existing producer loop. It uses the existing executor (SnapExec and run_check) in the producer's own build directory, and takes a build slot only if one is free (it never waits). A new failure, meaning one that did not time out and did not already fail on the base, joins the one existing send-back: its command, exit status and output tail are added to the send_back_text brief, and the stored invocation detail names it. PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS stays 1 and no loop was added. A check still failing after the send-back reaches the verifier as a flagged report gap. The criterion asked for GIT_INDEX_FILE to be set to a temporary index. The change instead uses that variable only to build the temporary index, swaps the index into the snapshot for the run, and never exports the variable to the checks. This differs from the wording, but D182 says so and gives a reason, and the accepted plan described it. I ran 31 targeted athena-core tests and all pass, covering the send-back with command and tail, the flagged still-failing check, the one-call happy path, a new file seen by `git ls-files`, base-failure filtering, the skips for tool configuration, low disk and a busy slot, and the CI-reuse baseline tests. The full athena-core suite passed. The full athena-cli suite passed on a clean run, and the only edit there (retry.rs) makes its assertion stricter. The brief and budget tests pass, D182 is a pure append whose Provenance bullet names the root cause, and the CHANGELOG entry is present. No changed file falls outside the deliverables list. Two minor findings: one earlier athena-cli run exited 101 while another suite ran alongside it (the failing test is unknown; a clean rerun and CI passed), and an interrupted run could leave the swapped index in place.
